note: Family-owned campground beside Horseleg Lake, a shallow non-motorized lake (paddle boats and canoes; the operator says it is not a great fishing lake); pool and mini golf. Many sites are seasonal. --Claude
summary: Operator pages: $39 (30 A W/E) / $42 (50 A) + tax, tent $25, phone-only reservations from April 1, season last weekend of April to early October (closed Oct 11, 2026). LONG-STAY concern: map shows a small 'Short Term Kamp' loop amid mostly named seasonal sites; seasonal sites sold out for 2027. Google 4.5 (209). Not waterfront kept.
flags: LONG-STAY / MOSTLY SEASONAL (reviewer decides): the operator's camp map labels one small loop 'Short Term Kamp' (about six sites: Ironwood, Locust, Hickory, Elm, Maple, Herring around it) among roughly 100 named sites; the pricing page sells two seasonal options ('Your R.V. can remain on your site all year'; '90+ nights ... for those of you who wish to stay full-time. A typical season is around 160 nights') and monthly sites ($750); the home page says 'All seasonal sites are sold out for 2027'. Five tests: (1) mostly seasonal - likely yes, from the map; (2) nightly price posted - yes, $39/$42 plus tax; (3) occupancy - phone-only booking, could not check; (4) nightly share - if only the Short Term Kamp loop takes nightly campers, ~6 of ~100 (under 1 in 10), but the map does not say the rest are all seasonal; (5) no lots for sale. Google 4.5 from 209 and RV Life 4.5/$$ (stored) do not trigger the review rule.
PRIVATE GATE: passes on price ($39-42 plus tax, operator page; no year given) and presence (own website with phone; Google Maps 4.5/209). No gateway needed (Minneapolis 57 km).

Season: stored opens 04-15 / closes 10-15 (derived from old note prose) contradicted: 'last weekend in April thru the first weekend in October', closed October 11 in 2026. opens cleared (the last weekend of April moves; it is in season.note), closes 10-11.

The map puts sites Trout, Marlin, Minnow, Lobster, Kingfish, Guppy, Flounder, Eel, Crow, Mackerel, Barracuda, Swordfish, Sunfish, Catfish, Northern and Sturgeon along Horseleg Lake (several tent icons among them), but imagery shows a tree line, then a wide band of marsh and floating vegetation before open water; no open frontage within ~50 m.
